newsitem.title: ITALY: Aeroporti di Roma says issue price 11,000 lire/shr.
newsitem.headline: Aeroporti di Roma says issue price 11,000 lire/shr.

text.p: Shares in Aeroporti di Roma, the first Italian airport operator to be privatised, will be priced at 11,000 lire in a public sale offer (OPV) next week, the company said in a statement after a shareholders' meeting.

The price came at the top of a range indicated in the company's sale prospectus of between 8,000 and 11,000 lire, and values ADR at 1.32 trillion lire. Italy's Stock Exchange Council had previously valued the prospective share price at 8,500 lire.
"Considering that in 1996, net profits were 90.2 billion lire, the price of 11,000 lire per share expresses a price earnings ratio of 14.6," the statement said.
"The price takes into account the indications of interest received from global coordinators at the roadshow."

ADR, which is now 73.58 percent owned by state industrial holding IRI, said it would sell 41 percent of the company or 49.2 million shares. That could be increased to 45 percent under a "green shoe" option in the case of extra demand.
ADR runs Rome's two airports at Fiumicino and Ciampino.
The public sale offer will be launched on July 15 and will close on July 16. Managing director Gaetano Galia said last week he expected the company to be listed on the Milan bourse on July 24 or 25.

ADR said 30 percent of the shares on sale would be offered to the public, five percent will be reserved for company employees, and 65 percent will be left for Italian and foreign institutional investors.
Lehman Brothers Holdings Plc, Italian bank Imi's LDV Holding B.V., Crediop B.V., UBS Capital B.V. and M.M. Warburg & Co., which indirectly own some 25 pct of ADR, will sell their stake.
With the offer, IRI's stake in Aeroporti di Roma will fall to around 54 pct, but Galia said last week that by 1998 IRI "will no longer be the main shareholder".
He added that a second tranche sale was planned but the amount had yet to be defined.

The global coordinator for the offer will be Lehman Brothers International (Europe) and co-global coordinator Cofiri Spa, while the OPV will be coordinated by Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino and Crediop.
Aeroporti di Roma boosted its net profits by 61 percent in 1996 to 90.2 billion lire and increased its turnover 11 percent to 1.16 trillion lire.
